deals.evidence: Now, Stoke City Holdings Limited, which holds a 98.1% stake in the club and owns Stoke City (Property) Limited in its entirety, has been demerged from bet365.
deals.headline: bet365 demerges Stoke City to John Coates and waives £90.5m of loans
deals.summary: bet365 demerged Stoke City Holdings Limited (98.1% of the club, plus Stoke City (Property) Limited) to chairman John Coates. Loans of £90.5m owed to bet365 were waived, leaving the club debt free, and the bet365 Stadium and Clayton Wood training ground passed to the club group.

name: Stoke City Football Club
notes: Revenue uses the BBC's report of the 2024-25 results (£35.4m); the club company's accounts at Companies House give turnover £35,438k, operating loss £29,537k and average league attendance 22,805, but that PDF is a scanned image (attendance evidence was read off the page image, so a text match on that URL will fail). The BBC's £30.9m operating loss and £60.8m pre-tax profit appear to be the announced figures including the £90.5m loan waiver; the club company's own operating loss is £29,537k. John Coates' holding in Stoke City Holdings is stated only as the band '75% or more'. No outside or institutional investor found; the Coates family has funded the club through bet365 and, since 2024, directly. Capacity is the Premier League's 2017/18 figure. Chief executive, shirt sponsor, kit supplier, wages and social counts not found on citable pages (stokecityfc.com renders client-side). No valuation published.

ownership_summary: Owned outright by chairman John Coates (co-founder of bet365) since a demerger from bet365 Group on 8 July 2024. Coates holds 75% or more of Stoke City Holdings Limited, which holds 98.1% of the club; the rest is held by a long list of small historic shareholders. The Coates family first became majority shareholders in the 1980s and again in 2006 through bet365.
